name: Emberflow-Hollow
description: Emberflow-Hollow is a world lit from below. Rivers of orange magma vein the basalt plains between three supervolcanoes whose calderas glow like open furnace doors, and the thin, scorched air shimmers above every vent field. Ash hangs permanently in the rust-colored sky, sifting down over everything in fine grey snow.

The surface hisses. Acid rain spits from low clouds and eats channels into the rock, while steam screams from a thousand fumaroles in a dissonant chorus that never resolves. In the lee of the rift valleys, where temperatures briefly dip below what most instruments call survivable, the rock wears slick coatings of black and ochre—living films of thermophile bacteria clinging to existence at the edge of boiling.

The mining consortium that hollowed the great shafts twenty years ago logged 'anomalous biological residues' in its final quarter and went bankrupt before anyone followed up. Their pressure-sealed complexes still stand, doors sealed against the heat, drills parked mid-bore beside ore faces laced with the same bacterial mats. Nobody has explained why the consortium's last transmission called the residue 'deliberate.'

What remains on Emberflow-Hollow may be the hardiest life ever catalogued, and it is dying—the supervolcano called Third Furnace is swelling, and when it goes the vent fields will be buried under fifty meters of ash. A biowealth syndicate wants samples before that happens; a smaller faction wants the whole biosphere protected in place, arguing the mats organize themselves into patterns too regular for chemistry alone. The clock on both arguments is measured in months.
